# Adjudication Task — Chapter 333

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃333화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“선화아(船火兒) 무송 대협께서는 잠시 기다려 주시겠습니까.”
  6|
  7|나는 목소리의 주인을 향해 기립박수를 쳐 주고 싶었다.
  8|
  9|생각해 봐라, 누가 지금 같은 분위기에서 저런 말을 꺼낼 수 있는지.
 10|
 11|더군다나 그 상대가 5분 동안 오십여 명의 수적들을 물고기 밥으로 던져 준 수적 두령일 경우에는 더더욱 그렇다.
 12|
 13|그런데 누구지?
 14|
 15|‘대협 운운하는 것으로 봐서 이쪽 계통은 당연히 아니고.’
 16|
 17|그의 수하들은 무송을 채주, 두령과 같은 호칭으로 부르니 제외. 나를 포함한 우리 일행 중 누구도 입을 열지 않았으니 그 역시도 제외다.
 18|
 19|그렇다면 남은 건…….
 20|
 21|‘수적에게 습격받았던 승객들인데.’
 22|
 23|이 자리의 모두가 나와 같은 생각을 떠올린 것이 분명했다.
 24|
 25|나와 일행들. 그리고 수룡채의 수적들까지. 사람들의 고개가 한쪽을 향해 쏠렸다. 황태구의 습격에 배가 기울어지자 쾌조선으로 옮겨탄 스무 명의 승객들을 향한 시선들이었다.
 26|
 27|“누구인가? 앞으로 나서라.”
 28|
 29|작살을 늘어트린 무송의 부리부리한 눈빛에 수하들이 황급히 길을 텄다. 그 끝에 한 사람이 있었다.
 30|
 31|“소인입니다.”
 32|
 33|목소리를 들었을 때부터 어느 정도는 예상했지만, 그는 상당히 젊었다. 아니, 앳되어 보이기까지 했다.
 34|
 35|‘많이 쳐 줘야 스무 살 정도?’
 36|
 37|청년이라기보다는 소년이라는 단어가 어울리는 그는, 사람들의 시선에 당황했는지 주춤거리다가 어설프게 양손을 모았다.
 38|
 39|“저, 저는 문경(文敬)이라 합니다.”
 40|
 41|“문경?”
 42|
 43|눈살을 찌푸린 무송이 물었다.
 44|
 45|“처음 듣는 이름이군. 보아하니 무림인도 아닌듯한데.”
 46|
 47|무송의 안목은 정확했다.
 48|
 49|그만큼 소년, 문경에게서 느껴지는 기운은 평범한 양민. 그 이상도 이하도 아니었다.
 50|
 51|자신을 훑어보는 우리의 시선에 마른침을 꿀꺽 삼킨 문경이 대답했다.
 52|
 53|“마, 맞습니다. 저는 아직 수련 중인 일개 의생(醫生)일 뿐, 무림과는 아무런 연이 없습니다.”
 54|
 55|“의생? 그런데 용케도 나를 아는군.”
 56|
 57|“사천의 장강에 의로운 뱃사공이 있어 살생(殺生)을 엄히 다스린다는 것을 어찌 모르겠습니까.”
 58|
 59|립 서비스 수준 보게.
 60|
 61|졸지에 사천 강줄기를 틀어쥐고 삥 뜯는 수적 두령에서 의로운 뱃사공이 된 무송의 입가가 씰룩거렸다.
 62|
 63|“으흠. 그런가?”
 64|
 65|“재물은 있다가도 없는 것이나, 목숨은 하나뿐인 것. 수년 전까지 장강에서 얼마나 많은 목숨이 사라졌는지 아는 이들은 무송 대협을 인의대협(仁義大俠)이라 부릅니다.”
 66|
 67|“커흠. 무슨 인의대협씩이나. 나는 장강의 영웅만으로도 족하네.”
 68|
 69|족 같은 소리 하네…….
 70|
 71|무송이 제법 개념이 박혀 있긴 해도 결국은 수적이다. 정도껏 양아치 짓을 한다고 해서 모범시민이 되는 건 아니지.
 72|
 73|하지만 저 어린 의생의 생각은 다른 모양이었다.
 74|
 75|“제 양친(兩親)께서는 십여 년 전 장강에서 비명횡사하셨습니다. 무송 대협께서 구해 주시지 않았다면 저도 같은 전철을 밟았겠지요.”
 76|
 77|“저런. 안됐군. 한데 십여 년 전이라면…….”
 78|
 79|“맞습니다.”
 80|
 81|문경이 떨리는 목소리로 말을 이었다.
 82|
 83|“지금 대협의 앞에 무릎을 꿇고 있는 저자가, 제 부모의 원수입니다.”
 84|
 85|“허어.”
 86|
 87|문경의 이야기에 집중하고 있던 수적들과 승객들이 침음성을 흘렸다. 감 잡았다는 듯이 고개를 끄덕인 무송이 입을 열었다.
 88|
 89|“내게 멈춰 달라 한 이유를 알겠군. 비록 본 맹의 맹규에는 어긋나나 그 마음을 충분히 짐작하는 바, 자네에게 기회를 주도록 하지.”
 90|
 91|“그의 생사여탈권을 제게 주신다는 말씀이십니까?”
 92|
 93|“물론일세.”
 94|
 95|하지만 뒤이어 들려온 문경의 대답은 나를 포함한 모두의 예상을 벗어나는 것이었다.
 96|
 97|“그렇다면…… 그를 살려 주십시오.”
 98|
 99|“……!”
100|
101|“……!”
102|
103|자신이 들고 있던 작살을 건네주려던 무송. 이미 모든 것을 체념한 듯 눈을 감고 있던 황태구마저 눈을 번쩍 뜨고 문경을 바라보았다.
104|
105|“뭐, 뭐라고?”
106|
107|당황한 표정으로 되묻는 무송에게 문경이 허리를 굽혔다.
108|
109|“부모의 원수를 갚고 싶은 마음은 굴뚝 같으나, 소인은 의생이옵니다. 생(生)을 다루는 자가 어찌 사(死)를 행하겠습니까. 다만 저자가 두 번 다시 악행을 저지르지 못하도록 무공을 폐하고 엄중한 법도에 따라 처벌하여 주시길 간청드립니다.”
110|
111|“자네 말대로라면 저놈은 맹의 본단(本團)으로 압송될 걸세. 죽어 마땅한 놈이지만…… 지금까지 뿌려 놓은 연줄로 목숨을 건질 수도 있어. 그럴 바에야 이 자리에서 직접 원한을 갚는 것이 낫지 않겠나?””
112|
113|“소인은 무림과 연이 없지만, 무림인에게 있어 무공을 잃는다는 것이 죽음과도 같다는 것은 익히 들어 알고 있습니다. 저는 그를 죽이지 않았으나, 이미 죽인 것과 다름없지 않겠습니까. 그리고…….”
114|
115|문경이 맑은 눈동자로 황태구를 응시했다.
116|
117|“이것은 개인의 복수가 아닌, 대의(代議)에 따른 것입니다. 장강수로맹이 직접 나서서 저자를 벌한다면 살육을 자행하는 다른 이들에게도 경각심이 생기지 않겠습니까.”
118|
119|소년의 의연한 목소리에는 이제 조금의 떨림도 존재하지 않았고, 듣는 이로 하여금 고개를 끄덕이게 하는 힘이 있었다.
120|
121|그런 모습에 지켜보던 사람들 사이로 탄성이 흘러나왔다.
122|
123|“허, 참. 어린 친구가 대단하군.”
124|
125|“나 같으면 당장 저놈의 가슴에 작살을 쑤셔 박았을 텐데.”
126|
127|“여러모로 난 놈일세. 좋은 의생이 되겠어.”
128|
129|무송도 일목요연한 말에 큰 감명을 받은 모양이었다. 감탄 어린 표정으로 고개를 끄덕인 그가 황태구의 앞에 섰다.
130|
131|“네놈도 귀가 뚫려 있다면 들었을 터. 어찌 생각하느냐?”
132|
133|“내, 반드시 살아남아 네놈들을 찢어 죽일 것이다.”
134|
135|황태구의 눈동자에 번뜩이던 살기는 그리 오래가지 못했다.
136|
137|퍽!
138|
139|“크헉!”
140|
141|황태구의 배꼽 아래. 단전(丹田)이라 불리는 그곳에 무송의 발끝이 꽂혀 있었다.
142|
143|무송이 차가운 시선으로 핏물을 토하며 뒤로 나자빠진 황태구를 내려보았다.
144|
145|“어디 한번 살아남아 네 뜻대로 해 보거라. 단전이 깨졌으니 살아도 산목숨이 아니겠지만.”
146|
147|심상치 않은 파공음과 함께 날아든 발끝이, 다시 한번 단전을 후려쳤다.
148|
149|후우우웅. 콰직!
150|
151|“커헉, 아, 안 돼!”
152|
153|황태구의 비명이 공허하게 울려 퍼졌을 때는, 이미 모든 것이 벌어진 후였다.
154|
155|스아아아.
156|
157|느껴진다. 꿈틀거리는 그의 칠공(七空)에서 흘러나온 기운이 허공에 흩어지고 있었다.
158|
159|물을 담고 있던 잔이 깨지면, 물은 밖으로 흘러넘치는 법. 기해혈(氣海穴)이 망가짐과 동시에 단전에 담고 있던 공력이 사라진 것이다.
160|
161|“네놈들을, 네놈들을 반드시-!”
162|
163|한때 수많은 선박을 거느린 채 사천의 장강을 주름잡던 절정 고수는 이제 존재하지 않는다.
164|
165|그저 힘없는 오십 대의 장년인이 된 황태구는 쉴 새 없이 외침을 토해 내다가 무송의 점혈로 뻣뻣하게 굳어 버렸다.
166|
167|“시끄러운 놈 같으니. 이놈을 적당한 곳에 처박아 둬라, 향후 본단으로 압송할 것이다.”
168|
169|“옛.”
170|
171|디그다를 닮은 구릿빛 머머리 수적 하나가 황태구를 업고 사라지자 모든 사태가 일단락되었다.
172|
173|무송이 뒤통수를 긁적이며 좌중을 쓸어 보았다.
174|
175|“이거 참. 못 볼 꼴을 보여 줬군. 이번 일로 고초를 겪은 분들께는 심심한 사과의 뜻을 표하오.”
176|
177|착한 수적이 나쁜 수적을 퇴치한 셈인가?
178|
179|어쨌건 수룡채의 등장으로 목숨을 건진 양민들이 허리를 굽실거렸다.
180|
181|“어이구, 아닙니다. 장강의 영웅분들이 아니셨으면 꼼짝없이 죽을 뻔했는걸요.”
182|
183|“이 은혜를 어찌 갚아야 할지…….”
184|
185|“원시천존께서 돌봐 주셨는지, 죽은 이도 하나 없으니 마음 쓰실 것 없습니다요.”
186|
187|어라? 한 명도 안 죽었다고?
188|
189|나는 누군가의 말에 문득 승객들을 훑어봤다.
190|
191|‘진짜네.’
192|
193|여기저기 다친 사람은 있어도 시체는 안 보인다.
194|
195|본격적인 백병전에 돌입하기 전 나와 무송이 도착하긴 했어도, 분명 원거리에서 화살이며 작살을 쏘아 댔었는데…….
196|
197|‘스물밖에 안 되는 양민들이 어떻게?’
198|
199|순간 떠오른 의문은 얼마 가지 않아 풀렸다.
200|
201|“저기 계신 어린 의생님이 없었으면 다 죽었을지도 모르지.”
202|
203|“암. 어떻게 그런 상황에서 저리 침착할 수가 있는지…… 참으로 대단하신 분이야.”
204|
205|두런두런 들려오는 대화의 내용은 이랬다.
206|
207|수적들이 다가오는 것을 발견한 사람들이 혼란에 빠졌을 때, 문경이 나서서 갑판을 뜯어 방패로 쓰게 하고 돛대를 부수게 했다는 것이다.
208|
209|‘갑판은 그렇다 치고, 돛대를 부숴?’
210|
211|보통 사람이었다면 죽을힘을 다해 노를 저어 도망칠 생각부터 했을 텐데, 문경은 달랐다.
212|
213|녀석은 돛을 부수어 마치 회오리치듯 출렁이는 장강의 거센 물살에 배의 운명을 맡겼다.
214|
215|‘그리고 성공했고.’
216|
217|수전(水戰)이 어떻게 돌아가는지는 대충 알고 있다.
218|
219|원거리 사격 뒤에 배를 바짝 붙여서 들이받거나, 밧줄 따위를 걸어 넘어가 백병전을 시도하는 게 기본 아닌가.
220|
221|하지만 그 대상이 방향 기능을 완전히 상실하고 빙글빙글 돌며 요동치고 있다면, 쉽사리 기회를 포착하기 어렵기 마련이다. 문경은 그렇게 시간을 벌었다.
222|
223|‘허, 이놈 봐라.’
224|
225|황태구에 관한 처분도 그렇고. 보통 영특한 놈이 아니다.
226|
227|그런 내 시선을 느낀 걸까, 자신을 향한 칭찬에 멋쩍게 웃고만 있던 문경이 움찔했다.
228|
229|“소, 소협. 제게 무슨 용무라도?”
230|
231|“용무는 무슨. 나이만 보면 내 동생뻘인데 참 대단한 일을 했구나, 싶어서 보고 있던 거지.”
232|
233|“과, 과찬이십니다.”
234|
235|“이야기를 들어 보니까 과감하던데. 그런 생각은 어떻게 한 거야?”
236|
237|“비록 지금은 의생의 길을 걷고 있지만, 부모님께서 돌아가시기 전에는 이것저것 잡서를 많이 읽었습니다.”
238|
239|“잡서?”
240|
241|“예. 이래 봬도 저희 집안이 한미한 무장 가문 출신이거든요. 조부님께서는 조정의 녹을 받던 군관이시기도 했습니다.”
242|
243|낯선 사람에 대한 미약한 경계심과 은근한 뿌듯함을 숨기려는 모습.
244|
245|이렇게 보면 저 나이대 소년과 딱히 다를 바도 없는데, 뭔가 찜찜하단 말이지.
246|
247|찬찬히 문경을 뜯어보던 나는 마음속으로 중얼거렸다.
248|
249|‘스킬, 기감 사용.’
250|
251|띠링.
252|
253|익숙한 종소리와 함께 녀석에 관한 정보가 허공으로 불쑥 솟아올랐다.
254|
255|
256|
257|[Lv.6 문경]
258|
259|
260|
261|“헛짚었네.”
262|
263|“예?”
264|
265|“아니야. 건강하고, 잘 먹고 잘 커라.”
266|
267|“예, 예에…….”
268|

In any case, the commoners whose lives had been saved by Water Dragon Stronghold bowed repeatedly.

[P91]
“Oh, no, not at all. Without the Heroes of the Yangtze, we would have been done for.”

[P92]
“We don’t know how we could ever repay this debt…”

[P93]
“The Primordial Heavenly Venerable must have watched over us. Not one person died, so please don’t trouble yourself over it.”

[P94]
*Huh? Not one person died?*

[P95]
At those words, I looked over the passengers.

[P96]
*It’s true.*

[P97]
There were injured people here and there, but no corpses.

[P98]
Mu Song and I had arrived before the battle turned into a full-scale melee, but the river bandits had definitely fired arrows and harpoons at them from a distance.

[P99]
*How had a mere twenty commoners all survived?*

[P100]
It didn’t take long for me to get my answer.

[P101]
“If that young medical apprentice hadn’t been here, we might all have died.”

[P102]
“Indeed. How could anyone remain so calm in a situation like that? He’s truly remarkable.”

[P103]
From the snippets of conversation drifting around me, I pieced together what had happened.

[P104]
When the passengers spotted the approaching river bandits and panicked, Mungyeong stepped forward. He had them tear up the deck and use the planks as shields, then ordered them to break the mast.

[P105]
*Tearing up the deck is one thing, but breaking the mast?*

[P106]
An ordinary person would have thought first of rowing for their life and escaping. Mungyeong had done the opposite.

[P107]
He had them bring down the sail and entrusted the boat’s fate to the Yangtze’s violent, swirling current.

[P108]
*And it worked.*

[P109]
I knew roughly how naval battles worked.

[P110]
After exchanging fire from a distance, the usual tactic was to close in and ram the other ship, or hook it with ropes and board it for close combat.

[P111]
But if the target had completely lost the ability to steer and was spinning and pitching wildly, finding an opening wouldn’t be easy. That was how Mungyeong had bought them time.

[P112]
*Well, look at this guy.*

[P113]
Then there was his decision regarding Hwang Tae-gu. This was no ordinary clever boy.

[P114]
Perhaps he felt my gaze. Mungyeong, who had been smiling awkwardly at all the praise directed his way, flinched.

[P115]
“Y-Young Hero. Did you need something from me?”

[P116]
“What would I need? Judging by your age, you could be my little brother. I was just looking at you because you did something impressive.”

[P117]
“Th-That’s too much praise.”

[P118]
“From what I heard, that was pretty bold. How did you come up with it?”

[P119]
“Although I’m training to become a medical apprentice now, before my parents passed away, I used to read all kinds of miscellaneous books.”

[P120]
“Miscellaneous books?”

[P121]
“Yes. Believe it or not, my family comes from a humble military household. My grandfather also served the imperial court as a military officer.”

[P122]
He was trying to hide both his faint wariness of a stranger and a quiet sense of pride.

[P123]
Seen this way, he wasn’t much different from any other boy his age.

[P124]
But something about him didn’t sit right.

[P125]
I studied Mungyeong carefully and muttered inwardly.

[P126]
*Skill, activate Qi Sense.*

[P127]
Ding.

[P128]
With the familiar chime, information about him appeared in the air.

[P129]
> **System**
>
> **Lv. 6 Mungyeong**

[P130]
“I guessed wrong.”

[P131]
“Pardon?”

[P132]
“Nothing. Stay healthy, eat well, and grow up strong.”

[P133]
“Y-Yes…”

[P134]
Clicking my tongue inwardly, I turned away from the bewildered Mungyeong.

[P135]
Mu Song, who had been watching, spoke quietly.

[P136]
“What was that about?”

[P137]
“Nothing important. I just took a personal interest in him.”

[P138]
“Junior, do you happen to have a taste for men?”

[P139]
*You fucking bastard…*

[P140]
When he saw my expression, Mu Song cleared his throat and changed the subject.

[P141]
“Ahem. In any case, we should continue on our way. The current is rough, but the wind is favorable, so we should reach Xi’an soon.”

[P142]
“What about the others? Their original boat was listing too.”

[P143]
“The others? Ah, my men will take them somewhere safe.”

[P144]
Mu Song chuckled and added,

[P145]
“Of course, we’ll accept a small token of their appreciation.”

[P146]
“……”

[P147]
Saving their lives, then shaking them down for money. Was that clever or stupid?

[P148]
I was briefly struck speechless by this novel form of creative economics when—

[P149]
“W-Wait a moment.”

[P150]
“Hm?”

[P151]
It was Mungyeong. Glancing around nervously, he fidgeted with his fingers before speaking.

[P152]
“Um, did you say you were going to Xi’an?”

[P153]
“That’s right. Why?”

[P154]
Mungyeong gasped, then spilled out his words in a rush.

[P155]
“The thing is, I happen to be on my way to Xi’an too. If you would give me a ride just this once, I’ll repay this kindness even beyond the grave, remember it to my very bones, and even if this body dies and dies, dies a thousand times over and turns to white bones, I will never forget—”

[P156]
*What is this?*

[P157]
I let out a long sigh at the Jeong Mong-ju villain.[^1]

[P158]
“Fine. Get on.”

[P159]
“Thank you!”

[P160]
As Mungyeong hurried off to gather his luggage, Mu Song muttered under his breath,

[P161]
“Wait, this is my ship…”

[P162]
*Yeah. No.*

[P163]
[^1]: Jeong Mong-ju was a Goryeo scholar-official remembered for a famous vow of loyalty in which he declared that even if he died a hundred deaths and his bones turned to dust, his loyalty would remain unchanged.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 333

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃333화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“선화아(船火兒) 무송 대협께서는 잠시 기다려 주시겠습니까.”
  6|
  7|나는 목소리의 주인을 향해 기립박수를 쳐 주고 싶었다.
  8|
  9|생각해 봐라, 누가 지금 같은 분위기에서 저런 말을 꺼낼 수 있는지.
 10|
 11|더군다나 그 상대가 5분 동안 오십여 명의 수적들을 물고기 밥으로 던져 준 수적 두령일 경우에는 더더욱 그렇다.
 12|
 13|그런데 누구지?
 14|
 15|‘대협 운운하는 것으로 봐서 이쪽 계통은 당연히 아니고.’
 16|
 17|그의 수하들은 무송을 채주, 두령과 같은 호칭으로 부르니 제외. 나를 포함한 우리 일행 중 누구도 입을 열지 않았으니 그 역시도 제외다.
 18|
 19|그렇다면 남은 건…….
 20|
 21|‘수적에게 습격받았던 승객들인데.’
 22|
 23|이 자리의 모두가 나와 같은 생각을 떠올린 것이 분명했다.
 24|
 25|나와 일행들. 그리고 수룡채의 수적들까지. 사람들의 고개가 한쪽을 향해 쏠렸다. 황태구의 습격에 배가 기울어지자 쾌조선으로 옮겨탄 스무 명의 승객들을 향한 시선들이었다.
 26|
 27|“누구인가? 앞으로 나서라.”
 28|
 29|작살을 늘어트린 무송의 부리부리한 눈빛에 수하들이 황급히 길을 텄다. 그 끝에 한 사람이 있었다.
 30|
 31|“소인입니다.”
 32|
 33|목소리를 들었을 때부터 어느 정도는 예상했지만, 그는 상당히 젊었다. 아니, 앳되어 보이기까지 했다.
 34|
 35|‘많이 쳐 줘야 스무 살 정도?’
 36|
 37|청년이라기보다는 소년이라는 단어가 어울리는 그는, 사람들의 시선에 당황했는지 주춤거리다가 어설프게 양손을 모았다.
 38|
 39|“저, 저는 문경(文敬)이라 합니다.”
 40|
 41|“문경?”
 42|
 43|눈살을 찌푸린 무송이 물었다.
 44|
 45|“처음 듣는 이름이군. 보아하니 무림인도 아닌듯한데.”
 46|
 47|무송의 안목은 정확했다.
 48|
 49|그만큼 소년, 문경에게서 느껴지는 기운은 평범한 양민. 그 이상도 이하도 아니었다.
 50|
 51|자신을 훑어보는 우리의 시선에 마른침을 꿀꺽 삼킨 문경이 대답했다.
 52|
 53|“마, 맞습니다. 저는 아직 수련 중인 일개 의생(醫生)일 뿐, 무림과는 아무런 연이 없습니다.”
 54|
 55|“의생? 그런데 용케도 나를 아는군.”
 56|
 57|“사천의 장강에 의로운 뱃사공이 있어 살생(殺生)을 엄히 다스린다는 것을 어찌 모르겠습니까.”
 58|
 59|립 서비스 수준 보게.
 60|
 61|졸지에 사천 강줄기를 틀어쥐고 삥 뜯는 수적 두령에서 의로운 뱃사공이 된 무송의 입가가 씰룩거렸다.
 62|
 63|“으흠. 그런가?”
 64|
 65|“재물은 있다가도 없는 것이나, 목숨은 하나뿐인 것. 수년 전까지 장강에서 얼마나 많은 목숨이 사라졌는지 아는 이들은 무송 대협을 인의대협(仁義大俠)이라 부릅니다.”
 66|
 67|“커흠. 무슨 인의대협씩이나. 나는 장강의 영웅만으로도 족하네.”
 68|
 69|족 같은 소리 하네…….
 70|
 71|무송이 제법 개념이 박혀 있긴 해도 결국은 수적이다. 정도껏 양아치 짓을 한다고 해서 모범시민이 되는 건 아니지.
 72|
 73|하지만 저 어린 의생의 생각은 다른 모양이었다.
 74|
 75|“제 양친(兩親)께서는 십여 년 전 장강에서 비명횡사하셨습니다. 무송 대협께서 구해 주시지 않았다면 저도 같은 전철을 밟았겠지요.”
 76|
 77|“저런. 안됐군. 한데 십여 년 전이라면…….”
 78|
 79|“맞습니다.”
 80|
 81|문경이 떨리는 목소리로 말을 이었다.
 82|
 83|“지금 대협의 앞에 무릎을 꿇고 있는 저자가, 제 부모의 원수입니다.”
 84|
 85|“허어.”
 86|
 87|문경의 이야기에 집중하고 있던 수적들과 승객들이 침음성을 흘렸다. 감 잡았다는 듯이 고개를 끄덕인 무송이 입을 열었다.
 88|
 89|“내게 멈춰 달라 한 이유를 알겠군. 비록 본 맹의 맹규에는 어긋나나 그 마음을 충분히 짐작하는 바, 자네에게 기회를 주도록 하지.”
 90|
 91|“그의 생사여탈권을 제게 주신다는 말씀이십니까?”
 92|
 93|“물론일세.”
 94|
 95|하지만 뒤이어 들려온 문경의 대답은 나를 포함한 모두의 예상을 벗어나는 것이었다.
 96|
 97|“그렇다면…… 그를 살려 주십시오.”
 98|
 99|“……!”
100|
101|“……!”
102|
103|자신이 들고 있던 작살을 건네주려던 무송. 이미 모든 것을 체념한 듯 눈을 감고 있던 황태구마저 눈을 번쩍 뜨고 문경을 바라보았다.
104|
105|“뭐, 뭐라고?”
106|
107|당황한 표정으로 되묻는 무송에게 문경이 허리를 굽혔다.
108|
109|“부모의 원수를 갚고 싶은 마음은 굴뚝 같으나, 소인은 의생이옵니다. 생(生)을 다루는 자가 어찌 사(死)를 행하겠습니까. 다만 저자가 두 번 다시 악행을 저지르지 못하도록 무공을 폐하고 엄중한 법도에 따라 처벌하여 주시길 간청드립니다.”
110|

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
